# ruleId: # EVERY line below carries `review-by:<YYYY-MM-DD>`. That is not decoration:
# tests/unit/zap-rules-have-review-dates.test.ts fails a PR if a suppression has
# no date, and the NIGHTLY job fails once a date passes — so a suppression
# cannot quietly outlive its reason, without a calendar date being able to
# redden an unrelated hotfix. (The expiry check deliberately does NOT sit in the
# PR-blocking unit suite; see that test's header.)
# ## Why this list is long, and why it has to be
# `cmd_options` no longer carries `-I` ("do not return failure on warning"), so
# ANY unsuppressed WARN now fails the job. `docs/security/zap-triage-2026-07-15.md`
# already accepted NINE rule ids with documented reasoning, and the reasons below
# are quoted from it rather than re-derived. Without them the nightly job would
# be red from its first post-merge run and every run after — turning the new
# Telegram channel into exactly the alert fatigue this change set out to end.
# ## The cost of a global IGNORE
# rules.tsv has no URL scoping, so each line also hides the NOT-yet-accepted
# variant of its own class. Two are worth naming:
#   10055 also covers the "CSP directives with no default-src fallback" finding
#         that was FIXED in the 2026-07-15 PR. Suppressing the id hides a
#         regression of that fix, so `tests/unit/csp-directive-floor.test.ts`
#         pins base-uri/object-src/form-action directly on the three configs —
#         that test, not the scan, is now what guards it.
#   10202 hides any future form-post surface that genuinely lacks a token.
# ## Removal plan
# 10055 and 10038 come OFF this list when the CSP nonce work lands
# (docs/security/csp-hardening-plan.md). Leaving them after that would hide a
# regression rather than silence a known residual.
